review_scope: Registered-source review of MARS via LASSO by Dohyeong Ki, Billy Fang and Adityanand Guntuboyina. The verified local source is arXiv:2111.11694v5, dated 13 October 2024, 108 pages. The title page has a Published in the Annals of Statistics header. Main text and references end on page 25; only the appendix roadmap and heading on page 26 were inspected, in a crop ending at y=181. No appendix body was used.
inventory: Seven actual Theorems: 3.1 on page 9, 3.2 on page 10, 3.4 on page 11, 3.5/3.6/3.8 on page 12 and 3.9 on page 13. All full statements fit on their listed pages and were compared with those rendered pages. Fresh enumeration of uppercase theorem headings covers all 25 main-text pages and distinguishes four ordinary-case references, Lemmas, Propositions and Remarks.
original_statements: Theorem 3.1 retains truth membership in the signed-measure MARS class, its complexity bound and lattice design (15). The expected empirical-risk bound has the full (sigma^2 V^{1/2}/n)^{4/5} factor, logarithmic exponent 3(2s-1)/5, additive sigma^2(log n)^2/n term and constants depending on rho,d.

Theorem 3.2 retains constants depending on m, the small-epsilon range, covering entropy under Lebesgue L2, epsilon^{-1/2}, logarithmic exponent 3(2m-1)/4 and the complete m=1 sentence omitting the logarithmic factor.
Theorem 3.4 retains the same truth and lattice assumptions but bounds the approximate estimator. Its additional term 8V^2/N^2, all variance/log terms and the definition N=min_k N_k remain complete.

Theorem 3.5 retains the squared population error rate in probability, n^{-4/5}(log n)^{8(s-1)/5}. It does not state an expected-risk bound. Its random-design and error assumptions are resolved from the preceding Section 3.2 prose.

Theorem 3.6 retains bracketing entropy, the square root of 4/epsilon, the absolute logarithm to power 2(m-1), every epsilon>0 and the complete final bracketing-number description. Its range is distinct from the small-epsilon covering theorem.

Theorem 3.8 retains the approximate estimator, both truth-class assumptions, N=min_k N_k=Omega(n^{4/15}), the explicit lower inequality and allowed dependence of c on B,d,V. The conclusion is the same population rate in probability, with every log exponent retained.

Theorem 3.9 retains the expected minimax-risk object in Fraktur M, constants with their distinct b,B,s and B,s dependencies, the log expression without an added 2, exponent 4(s-1)/5 and sample threshold c_{B,s}(sigma^2/V^2). The Gaussian and lower-density conditions from the preceding paragraph are archived separately.
source_passages: All 22 source entries and seven auxiliary passages were compared with rendered source pages. Positive parts, binary interaction supports and order, the unit-cube domain and original two-sided MARS basis match pages 1-2. The original infinite-dimensional class on page 3 uses only positive hinges, nonempty binary interactions of order at most s and finite signed Borel measures on half-open knot cubes.

The total variation definition uses countable measurable partitions. MARS complexity excludes the all-zero knot vector in each interaction measure, leaving the intercept and products of linear coordinates unpenalized. This is not an l1 bound on all coefficients. The exact estimator is any constrained argmin solution with V>0, as on page 4.

The observed-data knot sets on page 6 and their coefficient matrix in Proposition 2.2 are retained as auxiliary context. The exact coefficient objective (13) and reconstruction (14) are explicitly reused with changed J,M for the approximation. The original possible nonuniqueness and common fitted-value statement is complete across pages 7-8.

The approximate grids on page 8 use preselected positive integers N_k; their index set excludes the upper endpoint and the matrix uses l_k/N_k. Page 9 names the resulting reconstructed estimator. Its definition needs the restricted class and coefficient problem, not a chosen exact-estimator solution or the observed-data knot grid.

The fixed lattice on page 9 has n_k>=2, zero left endpoints, upper endpoints at most one and positive lower spacing rho/n_k; it need not be equispaced. The independent sub-Gaussian noise model does not assert identical distributions. Its risk is expected empirical error over responses with the design fixed.

The entropy class D_m on page 10 uses a signed measure on a closed cube with total variation at most one including zero. It has no extra free intercept and differs from the MARS complexity ball. Covering and bracketing terminology is retained with the conventional meanings and unspecified version details noted separately.

The random-design density is bounded above by B>=1; the iid mean-zero errors are independent of the iid design and have finite Lorentz L^{5,1} norm as defined by the tail integral. Squared population loss, minimax expected risk over all estimators and the further Gaussian/lower-density restriction match pages 11-13. The latter prose says bounded below, while its printed sup-norm inequality does not express that property; both are preserved.
dependency_review: All 32 direct uses, 62 related connections and 22 local dependency lists were checked. The two entropy statements depend on the signed-hinge class and their entropy functional, without regression or sampling assumptions. Risk statements do not inherit metric entropy, bracketing inequalities, integrated Brownian sheets or Hardy-Krause characterizations used in proofs. Fixed-design and random-design hypotheses remain separate. The approximate estimator uses the reused coefficient formulas with the expressly changed grid; it does not depend on the selected exact solution. The minimax lower bound ranges over all estimators and does not inherit either fitting algorithm or its computational grids.
names_and_highlights: Every interface title is backed by the original source wording, with no synthesized definition. All assumption passages keep their source kind and evidence. Selectors identify each source passage or label, and every additional selector occurs in a related same-paper statement. All related-theorem explanations follow the actual local paths. Independent PDF font checks confirm Fraktur minimax M, script risk/classes/grids and bold zero/one notation.
source_limitations: All 25 existing source notes are retained. They include signed-measure and half-open/closed-domain distinctions, unpenalized zero atoms, nonunique argmin and unspecified measurable selection, differing grid/count conventions, fixed versus random noise, the Lorentz versus fifth-moment condition, covering/bracketing convention details, expected versus in-probability risk, the differing approximation-grid rate scales, lower-density prose/formula mismatch and unspecified positivity ranges for rate logarithms. Appendix proofs and alternative smoothness characterizations are unnecessary to resolve the stored statements and were excluded. No proof certification or final-journal equivalence is claimed.

Earlier scripts are archived; the saved per-paper rebuild now resolves the fixed local PDF and reproduces every content artifact in an empty output directory without former temporary-file dependencies. The rebuild does not create a new source-review status.
